section.label: Exhibit 04
section.title: Letters for You
section.lede: I'm better at writing things down than saying them out loud. So I left a few letters here. Open whichever one you need.
section.hint: Click an envelope. They're not going anywhere.
section.note: Some are for today. Some are for the days after.

letters.seal: Open when you want to know what I see
letters.title: The Things I Notice
letters.subtitle: A letter about the small things
body: I don't think you realize how much of you I keep track of. The way you get quiet right before you say something you've been thinking about for a while. The little happy sound you make when the fries arrive. The way you say my name when you're tired.
I notice all of it. I don't always say so, because I'm bad at saying things out loud without making them sound smaller than they are. So this is me saying it plainly: you are very, very easy to love.
Not because you're perfect. Because you're you, and that turns out to be more than enough.

letters.title: For the Days You Forget
letters.subtitle: A reminder, for when your brain is being unkind
body: I wish I could stand in front of you on the days you're too hard on yourself and hold up a mirror that only shows what I see. You'd see someone kind, funny, stubborn in the best way, and so much more than whatever your brain is telling you at 2 a.m.
You don't have to be useful or cheerful or put together to be worth loving. You just have to be you. That's the whole requirement.
I'm not going anywhere. You can put this letter in your pocket and read it again whenever you need to.

letters.title: Happy Birthday, Love
letters.subtitle: The one I've been saving for November 15
body: I hope this year is gentle with you. I hope it brings the kind of days where you laugh until you can't breathe, where the fries are hot, where the shrimp is garlicky enough, where you fall asleep before you finish your show.
I hope I get to be there for a lot of it. And on the days I can't fix anything, I hope it's enough that I'm beside you while you figure it out.
Thank you for being born. Genuinely. The world got a lot better for me when you did.

letters.seal: Open if you want to smile
letters.title: Five Things, No Particular Order
letters.subtitle: Because you asked me once and I froze
body: Five things I love about you, in no particular order because they all take turns being my favorite:

1. The face you make when you're trying not to laugh. 2. How fiercely you care about the people you love. 3. Your taste in music — I stole Panata from you, and I'm not sorry. 4. How you turn a normal afternoon into something I want to remember. 5. The way you say my name. You can put that on my headstone.
There are about four hundred more, but this museum has a word limit and I have a reputation to protect.

letters.seal: Open when you need to believe me
letters.title: A Small Promise
letters.subtitle: My panata
body: I'm not going to promise you a life without hard days. That would be a lie, and you deserve better than a nice-sounding lie.

What I can promise is this: I'll stay. Through the boring parts, the confusing parts, the versions of us we haven't met yet. I'll keep choosing you on purpose, even when it's easy, especially when it isn't.
That's my panata. Yesterday, today, and after.

letters.seal: Open when you want to know what you changed
letters.title: The Day My World Got Brighter
letters.subtitle: A letter about what your existence did to me
body: Before you, my days were fine. They were quiet and they were fine, and I didn't know they were missing anything. Then you happened, and suddenly there was something to look forward to on a random Tuesday.

I adore you. Not in the soft, polite way people say it — in the way where I notice when you walk into a room before I notice anything else. You brought color to a world I thought was already colorful. You made ordinary things feel like they were worth paying attention to: your favorite song that I secretly listen to, a meal we didn't plan, late-night talks when the world is asleep and even when my eyes are tired — the love in my heart keeps me awake. Though I literally shut down sometimes, lol.
You didn't just enter my life. You lit it up. And I hope you never underestimate how much of my world only started existing because you were in it.
letters.signoff: Still a little in awe of you,

letters.seal: Open on the days you don't feel like enough
letters.title: You Are Not a Question to Be Solved
letters.subtitle: A letter about how you should see yourself
body: I need you to read this slowly, because I know your brain likes to argue. You are not a project. You are not something that needs fixing before it's allowed to be loved.

You should value yourself the way I value you: not for what you produce, not for how well you hold everything together, but because you are kind, thoughtful, funny, and so stubbornly good even when the world doesn't give that back to you. You deserve to be on your own list of people worth taking care of.

When you're being hard on yourself, borrow my view for a minute. From here, there's nothing to fix. There's just you, and you are enough on the days you do everything and on the days you can't get out of bed.
letters.signoff: Wishing you saw what I see,

letters.seal: Open when good things feel undeserved
letters.title: Every Good Thing, and Then Some
letters.subtitle: A letter about what you deserve
body: You give so much without keeping score. You check in when people go quiet. You remember the small things. You make room for everyone else, sometimes at your own expense. So let me say this plainly: you deserve every good thing that comes your way.

Not because you suffered enough to earn it. Not because you were kind enough to balance some cosmic ledger. You deserve good things because you are selfless in ways most people never notice, and kind in ways you don't even count as kindness.
So when something lovely happens to you, don't flinch. Don't look around for the catch. Open your hands, say thank you, and let yourself have it. If anyone has earned a soft landing, it is you.

letters.title: You Matter More Than You Know
letters.subtitle: A letter about the space you take up
body: There are people who move through the world leaving no trace, and then there's you. You leave traces everywhere. In my routines. In my playlists. In the way I check my phone, in the jokes only we understand, in the version of me that only exists because you've been around.

You matter to me on the loud days and the quiet ones. You matter when you're at your best and when you're convinced you're not. Your presence changes the temperature of a room, and it changes my whole week.

I don't love you in spite of who you are. I love you exactly because of it. So on the days you feel small, remember that in my world you were never a small thing at all. You're the reason it feels like a home.
letters.signoff: You are not a small thing to me,

letters.seal: Open when you need to hear it again
letters.title: A Thousand Reasons, and Still Not Enough
letters.subtitle: The letter I'll never finish
body: I love every interaction I get with you. The way your face changes right before you laugh, the way you react when you see something you like, the tiny pause before you answer a question you're really thinking about. I love your eyes most of all — how honest they are, how they say things you don't say out loud, how I could look at them for hours and still find something new.

And that's just one reason. There's the way you say my name, the way you care, the way you turn a boring afternoon into an event. The way you argue with me and then make me laugh. The way you show up. I could write a whole letter for every reason and still have more to write.

But here's the truth: no amount of letters will ever do justice to how much I love you. I could give you a thousand reasons and it still would not be enough. So let this one stand as proof that I tried — and that I will keep trying for as long as you let me.
